a: It hides many hardware details behind readable instructions
It can only run on a powerful computer
It executes directly without translation
It is always faster than every other language
tasks.fb: High-level describes the level of abstraction, not the speed or quality of the computer.

tasks.q: The Python example calculates 4 + 7. What does print(total) output?
a: total
tasks.fb: Both values are numbers. The addition produces 11, which is stored in total and then displayed.

tasks.q: Which level is each characteristic most closely associated with?
items: Usually easier for people to maintain
Closely tied to a processor instruction set
tasks.fb: High-level languages prioritise abstraction and readability. Low-level languages expose more hardware detail.

tasks.q: A programmer needs precise control of processor registers. Which is the stronger reason to consider a low-level language?
a: It exposes hardware operations more directly
It guarantees there will be no bugs
It runs unchanged on every processor
It is always quicker to develop
tasks.fb: Choose a language for the task requirements. Low-level code gives control, not a guarantee of correctness.

tasks.q: Which form of program instruction can a CPU execute directly?
a: Machine code for its instruction set
Python source code
An English description
Assembly mnemonics without translation
tasks.fb: A CPU executes machine instructions it recognises. Human-readable source code must be translated.

tasks.q: Select TWO accurate statements about machine code.
opts: Every CPU understands the same instructions
It is usually easier to maintain than high-level code
tasks.fb: Machine code is binary and specific to a compatible instruction set. A string of bits has no universal instruction meaning.

tasks.q: Match the description to the correct term.
pairs: Short instruction names such as ADD
Binary instructions executed by a CPU
tasks.fb: Assembly is source code too. It uses mnemonic instructions but remains close to the processor.

tasks.q: A simplified example loads 4 into R0, then adds 7 to R0. What value is now in R0?
tasks.fb: The register first holds 4. Adding 7 changes it to 11. This is an illustrative instruction model, not a specific processor syntax.

tasks.q: What does portable source code mean?
a: It can be used on different systems with suitable supporting software
Its file is always small enough for a memory stick
It requires no translation on any computer
It works without an operating system
tasks.fb: Portability is about using code across systems. It still depends on suitable software and any required libraries.

tasks.q: Does each statement about portability hold?
items: Python source needs a suitable runtime on the new system
Every machine-code program runs on every CPU
Hardware-specific code may need changes on a new processor
High-level code can depend on libraries that must also be available
tasks.fb: High-level code is often more portable, but the runtime, libraries and system features must still be compatible.

tasks.q: A school wants a revision app that staff can update easily. Which justification is strongest?
a: A high-level language makes the code easier to read and maintain
A high-level language guarantees the app uses no memory
Machine code is always easiest for staff to edit
Low-level code automatically works on all devices
tasks.fb: The requirement is easy maintenance. Link your reason to that requirement, rather than making absolute claims.

tasks.q: Select TWO sensible conclusions when choosing a language.
opts: Development time matters as well as execution speed
Different parts of a system can use different language levels
Low-level code is always the best choice
A high-level program never needs translation
correct: Development time matters as well as execution speed
Different parts of a system can use different language levels
tasks.fb: There is no best level for every project. Teams balance development effort, portability and hardware control.

tasks.q: Choose the best fit for each brief, using the stated priority.
items: A revision app: readable code and frequent updates
A tiny hardware routine: direct register control
A data report: rapid development using libraries
A processor-specific routine: fine control over instructions
tasks.fb: Use the priority in each brief. High-level code supports productive development; low-level code supports detailed hardware control.

tasks.q: Finish the recommendation by matching each choice to its reason.
pairs: High-level for a changing school quiz
Check before moving high-level source to another system
A compatible runtime and dependencies are available
tasks.fb: An exam explanation should connect a language characteristic to the requirement in the question.

info.title: High-level languages
info.text:
Use readable words and familiar operations to express a solution.

Hide many details of how the processor works.

Usually easier to write, understand and maintain.

Challenge: Why might a school choose Python to build a quiz?

Language level alone does not decide speed. The algorithm, translator, implementation and hardware all matter.

info.title: Low-level languages
info.text:
Close to the instructions and hardware of a processor.

Machine code and assembly are low-level languages.

Offer detailed control, but are harder to write and maintain.

Challenge: Why might precise hardware control matter in a device?

More control can mean more code and more details to manage. Development time and testing effort still matter.

info.title: Machine code
info.text:
Binary instructions that a compatible CPU can execute.

Each processor family has its own instruction set.

Difficult for people to read, write and check directly.

Challenge: Would the same machine code work on every CPU? Explain.

The binary diagram is illustrative. Actual instruction lengths and encodings depend on the processor architecture.

info.title: Assembly language
info.text:
Uses short instruction names called mnemonics.

Closely follows a particular processor instruction set.

Easier to read than binary, but still needs translation.

Challenge: Why is assembly low-level even though it uses words?

The register example shows the idea of assembly. You do not need to learn these illustrative instructions for OCR J277.

info.title: Moving between devices
info.text:
High-level source is often more portable between systems.

A suitable translator or runtime must be available.

Low-level code may need rewriting for another instruction set.

Challenge: What must be available before a Python program can run on a new computer?

Portable source code and a portable executable are different ideas. Reusing source may require translating it for the target system.

info.title: Choosing the right level
info.text:
Match the language to the requirements of the project.

High-level code can reduce development and maintenance effort.

Low-level code can provide fine control of speed and memory use.

Challenge: Give a language choice AND a reason for a school revision app.

For a stronger answer, name the requirement, choose the level, then explain how its characteristic meets that requirement.
